purpose: Non-windowed verification of Rust workspace preview content geometry and compilation of direct Metal preview canvases; no runtime GPU acceptance
build_consistency: final Ninja dry run reported no work to do
unit_verified_mechanisms: Rust places rows, section labels, split groups/tiles and explicit group/section gaps in data order. It reuses the live indentation cap and split geometry, including odd-width remainder distribution.

The source scroll offset is applied before viewport intersection; fully offscreen rows are culled and partially visible rows carry clipped bounds. Large/deep/narrow/zero-size/saturated inputs remain bounded.
The preview rows use the established Rust display-list recipe, retaining Unicode titles, monograms, active text and the close glyph without native Labels.
implemented_pending_runtime_verification: The Metal opt-in preview resolves tab/pin/tree data without creating WebContents. Up to three page canvases render the Rust display list with the existing shared device, queue, pipeline and 32-byte GPU quad ABI.
Each page uses a native visual-only viewport clipping adapter. Core Animation translates cached page drawables and supplies the 160ms final settle; platform event/focus/AX routing remains native.

Immutable scene captures redraw on first use, changed viewport/scale or drawable loss. Movement alone skips display-list generation and GPU submission. The preview retains at most eight scenes and resets scene/surface caches on viewport resize.

Only a complete GPU preview owns drawing. If any required surface is unavailable, every GPU page hides and the native paint-record path supplies the entire preview. A successful GPU preview does not invoke native snapshot capture.
Preview destruction removes both page views and clipping adapters. Workspace IDs, validation, commit callbacks, timers, reduced-motion policy and native fallback remain application/platform adapters.

The compiled checkpoint regression checks scene text, zero native captures, no new GPU submissions during simple translation, no WebContents creation before commit, commit/cancel and restoration of the normal Metal sidebar. It has not been executed.
deferred_checkpoint: Run the complete 44-case Metal matrix (prior 43 plus SwipePreviewUsesMetalWithoutNativeSnapshots) and the 17 Views controls against these rebuilt sources.
Exercise real clipping/scale/window motion, source scroll offset, folder collapse/deep nesting, split pairs, Unicode, momentum/phase-less streams, repeated gestures, reduced motion and final settle.
Force unavailable drawables/context failure and verify complete native fallback, then recovery; inspect cancellation/hide/window destruction and removal of native clipping adapters.
Package/sign and inspect the matching isolated app; run actual CPU/GPU/presentation comparisons separately. Unit test durations and submitted command buffers are not presentation latency.
limitations: Native Metal/Core Animation integration, visual correctness, input/AX interaction and performance are unverified until the windowed checkpoint. Compilation and Rust tests do not prove those behaviors.
Regular non-gesture workspace-switch animation still rasterizes native content. The native snapshot fallback and other Views surfaces remain; full functional migration is incomplete.
No new dependency, crate or framework was introduced. New animation APIs use the already-linked QuartzCore framework. Original-code Apache-2.0 and upstream notices are unchanged.
